b2-02-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Sounds in the Fog
b2-02-01.scenario: Rezeda Kázmér stands with you in a foggy street in old Pest and asks what you can hear.
b2-02-01.prompt: Tell Kázmér what you hear: the horseshoes on the cobblestones, and say that the wind from the Danube is cold.
cues: Say whose sound you hear and where it clatters
Say where the wind comes from and what it is like
b2-02-01.target: A macskaköveken kopogó patkók hangját hallom. A Duna felől érkező szél hideg.
b2-02-01.english: I hear the sound of the horseshoes clattering on the cobblestones. The wind arriving from the Danube is cold.
b2-02-01.canDo: I can form active present participles using the -ó/-ő suffix according to vowel harmony.

b2-02-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Man by the Window
b2-02-02.scenario: Szindbád sits in a coffeehouse in Pest and asks you which gentleman you mean.
b2-02-02.prompt: Tell Szindbád which gentleman you mean: the one sitting by the window in a coat.
b2-02-02.target: A kávéház ablakánál kabátban ülő úrra gondolok.
b2-02-02.english: I mean the gentleman sitting by the coffeehouse window in a coat.
b2-02-02.canDo: I can order multiple modifiers (place, time, manner, object) inside a pre-nominal participial phrase.

b2-02-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Yellowed Letter
b2-02-03.scenario: Rezeda Kázmér sees an old letter on Szindbád's table and asks you what kind of letter it is.
b2-02-03.prompt: Tell Kázmér about the letter on the table: it is carefully folded and has turned yellow.
cues: Say how the letter is folded
Say what has happened to its colour
b2-02-03.target: Az asztalon egy gondosan összehajtott, megsárgult levél van.
b2-02-03.english: On the table there is a carefully folded, yellowed letter.
b2-02-03.canDo: I can form and interpret past/passive participles (-t/-tt) as pre-nominal modifiers.

b2-02-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Summers That Never Return
b2-02-04.scenario: Szindbád sits with you in the old coffeehouse and asks what you remember of your youth.
b2-02-04.prompt: Tell Szindbád what you remember: the summers that never return and a scent that nothing else can match.
cues: Mention the summers and say they never return
Mention a scent nothing can be mistaken for it
b2-02-04.target: A soha vissza nem térő nyarakra emlékszem, és a semmivel össze nem téveszthető illatra.
b2-02-04.english: I remember the summers that never return and the scent that cannot be mistaken for anything else.
b2-02-04.canDo: I can combine active (-ó/-ő) and anterior/passive (-t/-tt) modifiers within a single rich sentence.

b2-02-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Vanishing Carriage
b2-02-05.scenario: At midnight you stand on the embankment with Rezeda Kázmér, and he asks what you can see in the dark.
b2-02-05.prompt: Tell Kázmér what you see: a red carriage that vanishes noiselessly in the dark.
cues: Say what colour the carriage is
Say how and where it vanishes
b2-02-05.target: A sötétben nesztelenül tovatűnő vörös postakocsit látom.
b2-02-05.english: I see the red stagecoach vanishing noiselessly in the dark.
b2-02-05.canDo: I can read an adapted passage from Krúdy's 'A vörös postakocsi' and answer questions about it.

b2-02-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: An Evening in the Coffeehouse
b2-02-consolidation.scenario: Szindbád asks you to describe the evening you spent in the old coffeehouse in Pest.
b2-02-consolidation.prompt: Describe the evening: say what the clock on the wall is like and what lies on the table.
cues: Mention the clock and where it ticks
Mention the letter on the table and how it looks
b2-02-consolidation.target: A falon ketyegő ingaóra nagyon hangos. Az asztalon egy megsárgult levél van.
b2-02-consolidation.english: The pendulum clock ticking on the wall is very loud. On the table there is a yellowed letter.
b2-02-consolidation.canDo: I can recognize and parse left-branching -ó/-ő and -t/-tt participial clauses in literary Hungarian.
